questions.question: Do you remember what book of the Bible we’ve been studying?
Do you remember what family we’ve been following?
What promises did God make to Abraham’s family?
questions.answer: To grow them into a great nation, give them a great land, and use them to bless the whole world.

questions.question: Who can tell us the names of this family of four?
Which of Isaac’s twin boys would get the blessing?

who was listening like a secret spy?
Who was that?
What animals did Rebekah send Jacob to go get?
What was different about their bodies?
questions.answer: Jacob had smooth skin; Esau was hairy.

questions.question: How did she make Jacob feel like his fuzzy big brother?
questions.answer: Dressed him in Esau’s clothes, wrapped goat skins around his hands and on his neck.

questions.question: He didn’t believe it was Esau until he did what?
Who did he think he was praying for?
What were those precious promises from God?
questions.answer: God would grow his family into a great nation, give them a great blessing, give them a great land to live in, and use them to bless the entire world.

questions.question: What was it?
questions.answer: Hunt for food, prepare a tasty meal for his dad.

questions.question: What did Isaac say he would do after eating Esau’s food?
What thoughts do you think went through Isaac’s mind when Esau said, “Hi, dad! Let’s eat. Then you can give me your blessing”?
When Esau found out that someone else had been given his blessing, what did Esau say?
How do you think Esau felt about this?
Why would his face be red?
Who remembers what happened with Esau’s birthright?
questions.answer: Jacob got hungry Esau to trade his firstborn rights for a bowl of stew.

questions.question: What was it?
questions.answer: After his father died, he would kill Jacob.

questions.question: how does the story of Jacob stealing Esau’s blessing teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.notes: Open or rhetorical question, no original parenthetical answer provided.

questions.question: What did Esau want to do when he found out?
How did God use Jacob’s family to bless the entire world?
questions.answer: Their many-times-great grandson Jesus died to pay for our sins, then rose from the dead.

questions.question: What does God promise to do for anyone who believes that Jesus died for our sins and rose from the dead?
questions.answer: Give them forever life in his good kingdom.

questions.question: Who hunted wild animals in today’s story?
What does that remind you of?
questions.answer: Isaac was blind and Jacob brought him a meal to eat.

questions.question: What did Isaac send Esau to go do?
questions.answer: Hunt for some food for his father to eat

questions.question: What was Isaac going to give to Esau after the meal?
Why was getting this blessing a big deal?
questions.answer: It came with all the promises God had made to Abraham and Isaac

questions.question: What tricky plan did Rebekah come up with?
questions.answer: To have Jacob pretend to be Esau and take the blessing

questions.question: What did Jacob do to fool Isaac?
questions.answer: Wore Esau’s clothes, wore goat fur, lied

questions.question: What did Isaac say when Jacob spoke?
questions.answer: The voice is Jacob’s, but the hands are Esau’s

questions.question: When did Isaac finally believe Jacob was Esau?
After eating Jacob’s food, what did Isaac do?
questions.answer: Give Jacob the blessing of God

questions.question: When Esau came in with his food, what did Isaac say and do?
How did Esau feel about what Jacob did? What did Esau plan to do?
questions.answer: Angry, he planned to kill Jacob

finishStory.markedParagraph: When [Isaac] grew old, he asked Esau to hunt and bring him food before receiving his [BLESSING]. While Esau was away, [Rebekah] made a plan to [TRICK] Isaac. Jacob put on his brother’s clothes and covered his hands with [GOAT] hair. Isaac could not see clearly, but he recognized Jacob’s voice. reviewFlags.text: Original memory verse is Romans 8:28a ESV with an ellipsis. All seven verse activities retain the source excerpt pending teacher choice and verification of exact BSB excerpt and reference, followed by synchronized re-selection.
Review 11 Multiple Choice questions and 22 newly authored distractors. Choose wrong answers that are plausible without becoming arguably correct. Original lesson questions are separately retained.
Check true/false truth, six selected deliberate false facts, and canonical fact-link consistency; facts used by Small True/False, Maze and Sort Story are not reused.
Odd Words and Checkboxes use plausible but unrelated Bible-story distractors rather than modern nonsense words. Confirm none accidentally belongs to OT15.
Review the six deliberately incorrect Circle the Mistakes statements, the ten-blank Finish Story, and chronological/drawing captions for age appropriateness and source accuracy.

The two Important Ideas on pages 5 and 6 are preserved verbatim. Teacher should review theological application, including the relationship between human deceit, sin, God’s promises and redemption, before publishing.
No live crossword/word-search grid placement, letter-puzzle engines, measured SVG/PDF layout, Review Studio 27-module preflight, or numbered worksheet preset tests have been run.
Only the 15-page ODT was provided. Referenced slides and printable resources were not separately supplied; generated prompts are based on the ODT narrative and displayed pictures only.
Review simplified matching pairs and crossword clues for uniqueness and classroom suitability; test that all crossword answers actually interlock.
